newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian securities attract strong interest in Jan.
newsitem.headline: Romanian securities attract strong interest in Jan.

text.p: Growing local and foreign investors' interest in the Romanian securities market took volumes and prices higher in January, brokers said.
An independent capitalisation-weighted index of the over-the-counter (OTC) market rose by 40 percent in January, said Vanguard SA securities in a statement released on Monday.
"From 1,000 points on January 6, the VAB-RASDAQ index went up by 40 percent to 1,380 points on January 31," it showed.
The VAB-RASDAQ is an index of all the stocks traded in the RASDAQ system -- Romania's equivalent of an OTC market, shaped on the U.S. NASDAQ exchange.
The system opened last October to trade shares in up to 5,000 companies from a mass selloff launched in 1995. It now lists over 2,000 stocks.
Vanguard, which also computes the VAB-BX bourse index, said the stock exchange had increased by 35 percent in January.
"Local investors showed renewed interest," said a broker. "They seem to trust the new cabinet's reform commitment and say there are enough attractive stocks to make the market advance."
Brokers also speak of foreign investor presence, which is a first. "We no longer have foreigners calling us to get a drift of our emerging market. Now, we have foreign buyers," said one.
Since last November's polls which ousted leftists, Romania has been ruled by a centrist coalition which has pledged capital markets and foreign investment support.

Traders have reasons to be pleased with the peformance of the market. A bull run had the bourse in its grip in January, pushing prices up at every session. Turnover on January 30 hit 802.9 million lei, the highest level this year and only second to an all-time record of 1.7 billion lei last March.
The RASDAQ was also buoyant. In the last week of January turnover quadrupled to 12.1 billion lei on the previous week.
"More than half the 212 stocks traded in January climbed and only 38 stocks went down," the Vanguard statement said.
But January's average prices of shares fell in real terms due to a weakened leu -- 45 percent down against the dollar.
"The market will grow more when the leu stabilises and we have a clear law on portfolio investment," an economist said.

Romania has no foreign portfolio investment law. Portfolio investors have to follow the same tedious procedures direct investors do, which puts a brake on market growth, traders say. ($=5,969 lei) -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
